Add an exchange rate or a price index

Source: R/currency-convert.R
add_currency.Rd

The shipped tables stop at the year they were built from. These add a row, or replace one, for the current session – a rate newer than the release, a currency the tables do not carry, or a deflator basis of your own.

Usage

add_currency_fx(code, year, lcu_per_usd, source = "user")

add_currency_deflator(
  code,
  year,
  index,
  basis = "gdp",
  area = NA_character_,
  source = "user"
)

Arguments

code

ISO 4217 currency code.

year

calendar year.

lcu_per_usd

units of the currency per US dollar. Note the direction: it is what the source series publishes, and the reciprocal of convert_data's coefficients. Adding one for a year the tables do not reach also adds the numeraire's own row for that year, which is 1 by definition, so a cross rate has both of its sides.

source

free text recording where the number came from.

index

a price index. Only ratios between years are used, so its base does not matter, but it must share a base with the other years of the same currency and basis.

basis

"gdp" or "cpi", or a name of your own.

area

the area the index is for, recorded for provenance.

Value

Invisibly, the added rows.

Examples

add_currency_fx("EUR", 2026, 0.92, source = "my own estimate")
convert("MEUR2026", "MUSD2026")
#> [1] 1.086957
